script.title: Offer vs Invitation to Offer
script.caption_hook: Price tag on a shirt: is the shop making an offer?

lines.say: Price tag on a shirt: who is making the offer?
Let's see. An offer shows willingness to be bound, if the other person agrees.
Once accepted, it becomes an agreement, which can become a binding contract.
So is the price tag an offer?
No. A price tag only invites offers. It does not bind the shopkeeper.
The customer, at the counter. The shopkeeper may accept or refuse.
Yes. Price lists, catalogues and tender notices are invitations. The bidder's tender is the offer.
The announcement invites offers. Your bid is the offer, accepted by fall of hammer.
No. An ad promising a reward to anyone who performs a condition is a general offer. That's the Carlill case.
Remember: Display equals Door. Offer, or bid, equals Bell. The customer's offer rings the bell.

check_notes: Writer: Fixed: accepted offer now becomes an agreement that can become a contract (Section 2(b)/Section 10); memory trick now says Offer (bid) = Bell, with the customer's offer ringing the bell. Board shows 'Offer = Bell' because of the 14-character limit; the spoken line says 'bid'.

Checker: Line 4 board (flow): the note '+ Section 10' is placed under 'Agreement', which suggests Section 10 is what makes an accepted offer into an agreement. Section 10 actually sets out when an agreement becomes a contract (free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration and object, not expressly declared void). Correct version: Offer → (Accepted) → Agreement → (+ Section 10 essentials) → Contract. Or relabel the note 'Contract if Section 10 is met'. Under s.2(b) and 2(e), strictly, an accepted proposal is a promise, and a promise backed by consideration is an agreement.
